newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says Bre-X, Barrick agree on Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says Bre-X, Barrick agree on Busang.

text.p: A top Indonesian mining official said on Monday that Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp had agreed on a government proposal for a 25-75 percent split of the spectacular Busang gold property.
"They have reported they can both accept the government suggestion," secretary-general of the Mines and Energy Ministry, Umar Said, told Reuters.
"They are also ready to provide a 10 percent stake to the government. It is good," Umar said.
The international mining community had watched with apprehension the turmoil over Busang, one of world's largest gold finds, fearing it could make doing business in Indonesia more complicated.
The issue concerned the small Canadian mining firm Bre-X and its stake in the Busang area, which it estimates holds at least 57 million ounces of gold in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province.

Bre-X had sought a partner to provide the funds needed to develop the jungle site on Borneo island. The costs and potential profits are huge -- the current value of the gold amounts to more than $21 billion.
The government had pressed Bre-X to link up with one of the world's biggest gold miners, Barrick Gold Corp. Two members of President Suharto's family are also involved in the long-running saga.
Asked why a decision was not made on the December 4 deadline for an agreement, Umar said the deadline had been extended at the request of Bre-X.
"We didn't make a decision because Bre-X asked for additional time to get the approval of shareholders. This is Canadian law," Umar said.
Umar had said earlier that if the two companies had failed to reach a partnership agreement, the government would explore other ways to expedite development of the Busang find.
